correctness.rationale: Differentiating the rational section integral along great circles gives the displayed log-second-derivative formula. At p_n the tangent representation splits into the standard zero-sum module and one collective direction; exact beta integrals give eigenvalues -3 and (n-8)/n. At q_n the tangent constraints force h_1=0 and the last-coordinate standard representation is irreducible, so symmetry makes the Hessian scalar; the inspected exact SymPy verifier reconstructs the rational factor and evaluates n=4,...,8 to the stated fractions. The argument is analytic for the sparse spectrum and exact finite symbolic integration for the stated dense cases.
residual_risks: No claim is made about the first nonzero higher-order term at p_8 or q_n for n>=9.
